entries.requirement: Every change must consider the SSH use case and never assume local-only execution.
entries.why: A change that only works locally breaks the remote host path the fabric exists for.

origin.quote: All changes must consider the SSH use case. Don't assume local-only execution.

entries.requirement: Clients and remote servers update independently, so a change to what a paired client and host exchange must treat mixed versions as the normal state.
entries.why: A wire change that assumes lockstep versions fails on the first old peer.

origin.quote: Clients and remote Orca servers update independently, so mixed versions are the normal state. Before changing anything a paired client and host exchange — RPC params, stream frames, or the content either side publishes over them — follow [`docs/reference/remote-wire-compatibility.md`](./docs/reference/remote-wire-compatibility.md). A new optional field is safe; a new stream opcode must be capability-negotiated because decoders drop unknown opcodes silently; and changing what the host publishes reaches old clients even with no wire change.

entries.requirement: Window close, client disconnect and app quit are Detach for remote executions: they never stop one or cancel a workstream.
entries.why: Treating a disconnect as a stop destroys work the owning host is still running.

origin.quote: Window close, client disconnect and app quit are Detach for remote and runtime-hosted Executions: they never stop one or cancel a Workstream. A local PTY owned by this app process is the exception: `killAllPty()` on will-quit and update install ends it with the process (pinned by `src/main/quit-path-local-runtime-teardown.characterization.test.ts`); daemon-backed PTYs survive. Stop Execution is an explicit act (`terminal.stopExact` and its siblings). Cancel Workstream belongs to UWCP (`uwcp.control/1`) and is ABSENT (refuses): `workstream.cancel` answers `workstream_authority_unavailable` and never degrades into a Stop. An RPC that launches or mutates an Execution declares `effect: 'launch'`. See [`docs/reference/detach-stop-cancel-effects.md`](./docs/reference/detach-stop-cancel-effects.md).

entries.requirement: A refusal of workspace consent is not a failure: the provider shows its own prompt, which is the control working.
entries.why: Pre-writing trust on a host forges consent the user never gave.

origin.quote: The gate lives in the four producer functions, not in their callers. The effect has five call sites across desktop launch prep, desktop resume, a renderer-callable IPC channel, remote worktrees and the runtime/headless host; guarding callers would fence those five and leave every future one open. A refusal is not a failure — the provider shows its own prompt, which is the control working. There is no product grant surface yet, so today every call degrades that way.

entries.requirement: A live leg on the owning host restores the service home: SVC_HOME_RESTORED must read True after the run.
entries.why: A leg that leaves the account home changed contaminates the next host run.

entries.requirement: A live leg leaves no claude projects behind on the owning host: HWF_CLAUDE_PROJECTS must read 0.
entries.why: Stray project records on the service account change what later sessions resume.
